newsitem.title: USA: Intel CEO's 1996 compensation rose 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Intel CEO's 1996 compensation rose 11 pct.

text.p: Intel Corp Monday said Chief Executive Andrew Grove earned $3.35 million last year, up 11 percent from the previous year.

In its annual proxy statement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Intel said Grove also received options of 72,00 shares of stock that could be worth another $7 million if Intel's stock rises 10 percent a year over the next 10 years.
Intel, the world's largest semiconductor maker, said Grove earned a base salary of $425,000 in 1996, a bonus of $2.58 million and other cash compensation totaling $347,500.
That compared with a base salary of $400,000 in 1995, a bonus of $2.36 million and other cash compensation of $266,100.

Since 1991, Intel's shares have risen sharply, outperforming the S&P 500 index and the Dow Jones Technology Index. The company said an investment of $100 in Intel stock in 1991 would be worth $1,156 in 1996.
